source_review.notes: Checked all ten structured references. Current CNCF and DORA pages support user-centered, journey, task-success, adoption, delivery, and balanced platform-outcome claims; DORA's errata confirms v.2024.3 as the latest corrected 2024 report. Current Strategyzer guidance supports the jobs/pains/gains framing. GOV.UK discovery, benefits, and performance guidance supports end-to-end research, baselines, segmentation, costs, iteration, and stopping. ISO confirms ISO 9241-210:2019 remained current after its 2025 review. Books are used as practitioner frameworks, not empirical proof.

evidence: Checked V=(U,J,K,A,C,M,O,T,E,G,R,S), Y_0, Y_1, delta Y, B_c, B_p, B_o, and the causal chain against first-use definitions and Definitions and Notation.
Checked display delimiters, subscripts, arrows, Delta syntax, and inline math with the repository GitHub-math validator.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Every symbol is defined and scoped. The twelve-element value tuple remains consistent in the review, exposition, definitions, exercises, and answers.

evidence: Recomputed four hypothesis records, two structurally ready records, and three unique segments.
Recomputed exactly one missing baseline and one missing stop condition.
Executed value-hypothesis-gate with python3; observed output matched every declared line exactly.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable gate supplies the chapter's derived counts. Times and percentages in narrative examples are stated scenario inputs rather than calculated empirical findings.

evidence: Expanded all twelve V tuple components against the readable hypothesis template.
Checked delta Y=Y_1-Y_0 and verified the text explicitly separates observed difference from causal effect.
Checked the capability-to-mechanism-to-task-to-delivery-to-organization chain and decreasing attribution strength.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The notation organizes hypotheses and review; it does not claim that unlike burdens are directly additive or that observed differences establish causality.

evidence: Reviewed novice-benefit/expert-slowdown, faster-creation/slower-recovery, adoption/mandate, consumer-saving/operator-toil, standardization/bypass, average/accessibility, local-cost/concentration, satisfaction/task-failure, and concurrent-change cases.
Checked ticket, local automation, provider-direct, enablement, managed capability, no-build, delay, and abandonment alternatives.
Checked rare high-consequence pain, frequent minor pain, unsupported workloads, and retirement boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The chapter challenges happy-path, average, coercive-adoption, over-attribution, burden-transfer, and false-precision claims while preserving legitimate strategic and non-monetized value.

evidence: Traced segment, job, context, alternative, mechanism, outcome, horizon, evidence, guardrails, obligations, and stopping through the full chapter.
Checked that baselines and eligible denominators precede adoption and improvement interpretations.
Checked consumer, organizational, operator, affected-party, lifecycle, and opportunity-cost perspectives.
invariant_checking.notes: The proposition remains falsifiable and counterfactual throughout. No feature, roadmap item, mandate, satisfaction score, or adoption count is accepted alone as proof of value.

proof_review.notes: The chapter states no formal theorem and contains no deductive proof. Its equations are hypothesis, observed-difference, burden-review, and causal-chain notation.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No proof sketch is claimed. The text explicitly disclaims causal proof from delta Y and direct summation of unlike burdens.

evidence: The hypothesis gate is labeled synthetic and limited to structural completeness.
DORA findings are attributed and paired with mixed-effect and survey limitations rather than universal causal claims.
All worked-example numbers are framed as scenario evidence, and the causal-chain section requires competing explanations and bounded attribution.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Practitioner frameworks, current guidance, survey findings, synthetic computation, local observations, and causal claims are kept distinct. No external review or universal ROI is claimed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter consistently distinguishes value proposition from vision, feature list, mandate, roadmap, and business case; separates jobs, pains, gains, constraints, mechanisms, outcomes, and evidence; and treats value as segment-specific, counterfactual, lifecycle-bound, and distributed across consumers, organization, operators, and affected parties.

practitioner_review.notes: A practitioner can use the twelve-field hypothesis, current-journey baseline, mechanism chain, four evidence layers, metric specification, alternative comparison, burden-transfer review, and stop criteria. Examples cover mandates, expert users, recovery regression, cost transfer, accessibility, security authority, rare specialist work, attribution, and retirement.

pedagogical_review.notes: The sequence moves from segment/job and current alternative through hypothesis, mechanism, evidence, stakeholder value, measures, alternatives, and stopping. Ten examples remain distinct; five exercises progress from rewriting a slogan through baseline design, conflicting evidence, alternative choice, and safety-critical transfer, with complete assumption-aware answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
